approachQuestion.prompt:
Check the Seat Assignment

An array seats of length n claims to list every seat number from 0 through n−1 exactly once. Return whether that claim is true. Values may be repeated or out of range; do not assume the claim in advance.

Example 1: seats=[2,0,3,1] → true.
Example 2: seats=[0,1,1] → false.
Example 3: seats=[0,3,1] → false.

Constraints:
1 ≤ n=seats.length ≤ 200,000; −10^9 ≤ seats[i] ≤ 10^9.
Do not modify seats. Return one Boolean.
Seat numbers are ordinary fixed-width integers.
constraints: Do not modify seats. Return one Boolean.
Seat numbers are ordinary fixed-width integers.

options.text: Allocate n false flags. For each value v, reject if v is outside 0..n−1 or flag[v] is already true; otherwise set it. Accept after all n values.
options.feedback: Within a domain of n possible values, n distinct in-range entries must cover every seat. Range checking before indexing prevents invalid access.

options.text: Copy seats, sort the copy, then check that the value at every index i is i.
options.feedback: This validates the entire claim and preserves the original, but sorting does avoidable ordering work when a direct-address flag array can detect repeated or invalid values.

options.text: Accept exactly when the sum of the values equals n*(n−1)/2, without checking individual values or repetitions.
options.feedback: A matching sum does not ensure distinctness or range. [1,1,1] has the target sum 3 for n=3 but is not a valid assignment.

options.text: Accept if every value lies between 0 and n−1.
options.feedback: Range membership does not prevent repeated seats. [0,0] passes this check but omits seat 1.

feedback.reason: Check the legal range before indexing the flags, then reject any flag already set.
details: Allocate a false flag for every legal seat. Check the range before using a value as an index, then reject a flag already set or set a new flag. Accept after the complete scan.

Check the legal range before indexing the flags, then reject any flag already set. With n in-range distinct seats drawn from exactly n legal seats, coverage follows from uniqueness; no second coverage structure is needed. A duplicate necessarily leaves some other seat unassigned.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Mark Each Legal Seat Once”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be seats.length. Flag allocation initializes n entries and costs linear time; integer comparison and direct indexed access cost constant time. Exclude input and Boolean output; include flags, helper variables and stack. No hashing, recursion or copying of the input is used.
constraints: Do not modify seats. Return one Boolean.
Seat numbers are ordinary fixed-width integers.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Initialize n flags and scan n assignments using direct addressing.
details: Initializing n flags and visiting at most n input values take linear time. The flags occupy n helper entries; they are not output. Direct addressing uses the stated integer range, with no probabilistic hashing assumption.
The option “O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.”: The indexed flags are both sufficient and linear in n.
The option “O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: This omits the n-entry helper flag array.
The option “O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.”: Sorting belongs to a different method, not direct marking.
The option “O(1) time, O(n) auxiliary space.”: Allocation and potentially the full scan are required.
